results.name: Cable One Arm Inner Biceps Curl
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, keeping your back straight, with your right side facing the machine, holding the handle with your right hand, arm extended at shoulder height parallel to the floor, palm facing up.
Curl the handle towards your shoulder by bending your elbow, keeping your upper arm stationary and parallel to the floor.
Slowly extend your arm back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to your left hand.
tips: Focus on squeezing your biceps at the top of the movement.
Exhale as you curl the handle up and inhale as you extend it back.
Keep your elbow at shoulder height and stationary throughout the exercise.
results.description: Cable One Arm Inner Biceps Curl is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Shoulders.

results.name: Cable Overhead Curl
instructions: Stand in the center of a cable machine with the pulleys set at the highest position. Grasp the handles with both hands, palms facing upward. Extend your arms out to the sides at shoulder height, almost parallel to the floor.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, keeping your back straight and elbows slightly bent.
Curl the handles towards your head by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Slowly extend your arms back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you curl the handles towards your head and inhale as you extend them back.
Keep your elbows stationary and at shoulder height throughout the exercise.
Focus on squeezing your biceps at the top of the movement.
results.description: Cable Overhead Curl is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Forearms.

results.name: Cable Preacher Curl
instructions: Sit on the preacher bench with your feet flat on the floor. Attach a straight bar to the low pulley of a cable machine and grasp the bar with both hands, shoulder-width apart, palms facing upwards.
Position your upper arms on the preacher bench pad and extend your arms fully, holding the bar.
Curl the bar towards your shoulders by bending your elbows, squeezing your biceps at the top of the movement.
Lower the bar back to the starting position, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you curl the bar up and inhale as you lower it back down.
Maintain a neutral wrist position to prevent strain.
Focus on squeezing your biceps at the top of the movement.
results.description: Cable Preacher Curl is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Cable Reverse Curl
instructions: Stand facing the cable machine with a straight bar attached to the low pulley. Grasp the bar with both hands using an overhand grip (palms facing down), hands shoulder-width apart.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, keeping your back straight and arms fully extended down in front of you.
Curl the bar upwards towards your shoulders by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary and close to your body.
Slowly lower the bar back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you curl the bar up and inhale as you lower it back down.
Use a lighter weight to ensure proper form and gradually increase the resistance as you get stronger.
Focus on squeezing your biceps at the top of the movement.
results.description: Cable Reverse Curl is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Cable Twisting Biceps Curl
instructions: Stand slightly sideways to a low cable pulley and hold the handle with one hand using a neutral grip. Keep your elbow close to your side and your arm fully extended.
Curl the handle toward your shoulder while rotating your forearm from a neutral grip into a supinated grip as your elbow bends.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement with your palm facing upward while squeezing your biceps.
Slowly lower the handle back to the starting position while rotating your forearm back to a neutral grip. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching sides.
tips: Keep your elbow close to your side throughout the movement and avoid using momentum to curl the weight up.
Perform the movement smoothly to maintain constant tension throughout the exercise.
Finish each repetition with a fully supinated grip to maximize biceps contraction.
Inhale as you lower the handle and exhale as you curl it upward.
results.description: Cable Twisting Biceps Curl is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms, Shoulders.

results.name: Concentration Curls Dumbbell
instructions: Sit on a bench with your legs spread apart. Hold a dumbbell in your right hand and rest your right elbow on the inside of your right thigh.
Let the dumbbell hang down towards the floor with your arm fully extended.
Curl the dumbbell towards your shoulder by contracting your biceps, keeping your elbow stationary and close to your thigh. Squeeze the biceps at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position, fully extending your arm. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the left arm.
tips: Focus on squeezing the biceps at the top of the movement to maximize muscle activation.
Ensure your back remains straight and avoid leaning back as you lift the weight.
Use a weight that allows you to perform the exercise with proper form and without straining.
results.description: Concentration Curls Dumbbell is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Doorway Biceps Curl
instructions: Stand in a doorway and grip the sides of the door frame at about hip height, palms facing forward or slightly inward depending on comfort and doorway design.
Step forward with one foot to create tension in your arms and lean slightly back, so your body weight helps create resistance.
Curl your elbows to raise your body slowly towards the door frame, keeping your elbows pinned at your sides.
Slowly extend your arms back to the starting position, repeat the movement.
tips: Ensure your grip is firm and your hands are positioned comfortably to avoid strain on your wrists.
Keep your body straight and avoid swinging; the motion should come solely from your biceps.
Adjust the position of your feet to increase or decrease resistance—the further you step and lean back, the harder the curl.
results.description: Doorway Biceps Curl is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Drag Curl Dumbbell
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with an underhand grip (palms facing up). Let your arms hang straight down by your sides.
Begin by dragging the dumbbells upward along your torso by bending your elbows and pulling them back, as if you are zipping up your jacket.
Continue lifting the dumbbells until they reach chest height, focusing on squeezing your biceps at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position, maintaining control throughout the descent. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on the mind-muscle connection, feeling the contraction in your biceps throughout the movement.
Use a weight that allows you to perform the exercise with proper form without straining.
Avoid using momentum; perform the exercise in a slow and controlled manner.
results.description: Drag Curl Dumbbell is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Drag Curl Resistance Band
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place a resistance band under your feet. Hold the handles of the band with both hands, palms facing forward.
Keep your elbows close to your body and your back straight. Start with your arms fully extended down at your sides.
Curl the handles up by dragging your elbows along your torso, keeping them close to your torso, until your hands reach chest level.
Slowly lower the handles back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you curl the handles up and inhale as you lower them back down.
Use a lighter resistance band if needed to ensure proper form and gradually increase the resistance as you get stronger.
Focus on engaging your biceps throughout the movement.
results.description: Drag Curl Resistance Band is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Shoulders.

results.name: Dumbbell Seated Alternate Biceps Curl
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your arms fully extended by your sides and palms facing inwards.

Keep your elbows close to your torso and curl the right dumbbell towards your shoulder by contracting your biceps. Rotate your forearm as you lift the dumbbell so that your palm faces your shoulder at the top of the movement.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat the movement with your left arm while keeping the right arm extended. Continue alternating arms for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your elbows stationary and close to your torso to isolate the biceps.
Avoid using momentum or swinging your body to lift the dumbbells.
Breathe out as you curl the dumbbell up and breathe in as you lower it.
results.description: Dumbbell Seated Alternate Biceps Curl is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.
